COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENT

between

RIDGELINE AEROSPACE COMPONENTS, INC.
(the "Employer")

and

INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF PRECISION MACHINISTS, LOCAL 418
(the "Union")

Effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2029

ARTICLE 1 — RECOGNITION

The Employer recognizes the Union as the exclusive bargaining representative for all full-time and regular part-time production and maintenance employees at the Employer's Rockford, Illinois facility, excluding office clerical employees, professional employees, guards, and supervisors as defined in the National Labor Relations Act.

ARTICLE 2 — UNION SECURITY AND DUES

Employees covered by this Agreement shall, as a condition of continued employment, become and remain members in good standing of the Union or pay the Union a service fee, on or after the thirtieth (30th) day following the beginning of employment, to the extent permitted by applicable law. The Employer shall deduct Union dues from the wages of each employee who has signed a written authorization, and shall remit them to the Union monthly. The Union shall indemnify and hold the Employer harmless from any claim arising out of deductions made in reliance on such authorizations.

ARTICLE 3 — MANAGEMENT RIGHTS

Except as expressly limited by this Agreement, the Employer retains the exclusive right to manage its business, including the right to direct the workforce; to hire, promote, transfer, and assign; to discipline and discharge for just cause; to determine the methods, processes, and equipment used; to establish and change work schedules; and to introduce new or improved methods or facilities.

ARTICLE 4 — NO STRIKE, NO LOCKOUT

During the term of this Agreement, the Union shall not authorize, sanction, or condone any strike, slowdown, work stoppage, or other interruption of work, and the Employer shall not lock out employees. Nothing in this Article limits the right of any employee to engage in activity protected by Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act that is not inconsistent with this Article.

ARTICLE 5 — SENIORITY

Seniority means an employee's length of continuous service with the Employer within the bargaining unit. Seniority governs layoff, recall, shift preference, and vacation scheduling, provided the senior employee has the present ability to perform the available work. Seniority is broken by voluntary quit, discharge for just cause, layoff exceeding twenty-four (24) months, or failure to return from recall within five (5) working days after notice.

ARTICLE 6 — WAGES

Wage rates for each classification are set out in Appendix A. Effective the first full pay period of each contract year, all rates increase by three percent (3%), three percent (3%), and two and one-half percent (2.5%) respectively. Employees assigned to a higher classification for more than four (4) hours in a shift receive the higher rate for the entire shift.

ARTICLE 7 — HOURS AND OVERTIME

The normal workweek is forty (40) hours, Monday through Friday. Time and one-half is paid for hours worked in excess of eight (8) in a day or forty (40) in a week, and double time for hours worked on Sunday and on the holidays listed in Article 9. Overtime is offered by seniority within classification and is not pyramided.

ARTICLE 8 — HEALTH AND WELFARE

The Employer shall contribute to the Precision Machinists Health and Welfare Fund at the rate of $9.75 per compensable hour. The Employer's obligation is limited to the contributions required by this Article, and the Trustees of the Fund administer the plan of benefits.

ARTICLE 9 — HOLIDAYS AND VACATION

Employees receive eleven (11) paid holidays per contract year, listed in Appendix B. Vacation accrues at one (1) week after one year of service, two (2) weeks after three years, three (3) weeks after eight years, and four (4) weeks after fifteen years.

ARTICLE 10 — GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION

Step 1. An employee with a grievance shall present it, with the steward, to the immediate supervisor within ten (10) working days after the employee knew or should have known of the events giving rise to it. The supervisor shall answer within five (5) working days.

Step 2. If unresolved, the Union shall submit the grievance in writing to the Plant Manager within five (5) working days after the Step 1 answer. The Plant Manager shall answer in writing within ten (10) working days.

Step 3. If unresolved, either party may submit the grievance to arbitration by written notice within twenty (20) working days after the Step 2 answer. The parties shall select an arbitrator from a panel furnished by the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service. The arbitrator's decision is final and binding on the Employer, the Union, and the affected employees. The arbitrator has no authority to add to, subtract from, or modify this Agreement. The fees and expenses of the arbitrator are shared equally.

ARTICLE 11 — DISCIPLINE AND DISCHARGE

No employee who has completed the probationary period shall be disciplined or discharged except for just cause. The Employer shall apply progressive discipline — verbal warning, written warning, suspension, discharge — except for offenses warranting immediate discharge. The Employer shall notify the Union in writing within two (2) working days of any suspension or discharge, and the employee is entitled to union representation at any investigatory interview the employee reasonably believes may result in discipline.

ARTICLE 12 — HEALTH AND SAFETY

The Employer shall provide a safe workplace in compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act and applicable state law. A joint labor-management safety committee, with equal representation, shall meet monthly and may inspect the facility. No employee shall be disciplined for refusing work the employee reasonably and in good faith believes poses an imminent danger of death or serious physical harm.

ARTICLE 13 — NON-DISCRIMINATION

Neither the Employer nor the Union shall discriminate against any employee on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, union activity, or any other characteristic protected by law.

ARTICLE 14 — SUCCESSORS

This Agreement is binding on the Employer's successors and assigns. The Employer shall give the Union thirty (30) days written notice of any sale, merger, or transfer of the facility and shall disclose the existence of this Agreement to the purchaser.

ARTICLE 15 — SAVINGS AND ENTIRE AGREEMENT

If any provision is held invalid, the remainder continues in effect and the parties shall meet within thirty (30) days to negotiate a replacement. This Agreement is the complete agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior agreements and practices except those expressly preserved.

ARTICLE 16 — TERM

This Agreement is effective March 1, 2026 and continues through February 28, 2029, and from year to year thereafter unless either party gives written notice of termination or of a desire to modify at least sixty (60) days before the expiration date.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement.

RIDGELINE AEROSPACE COMPONENTS, INC.
